name: Orki Doctor Profile & Appointment Booking
author: swarnodigital

sections.description:
Build a doctor directory for a clinic, hospital or medical group, and let patients find a doctor and book a real time from the doctor’s OPD schedule.

Doctors and profiles

  • Every doctor detail is a field you create: text, numbers, dates, dropdowns, checkboxes, images, galleries, files, rich text, repeaters and more (24 types). Nothing is predefined.
  • Choose per field where it shows: listings, profile, search results, or nowhere (“Internal only” keeps a field for staff).
  • Each doctor gets a profile page in a ready-made layout, or in your own design (built in Elementor or the block editor) used for every doctor. The theme’s own page title and post details are hidden on doctor pages, so the doctor’s name is shown once.
  • Doctor lists as vertical cards, horizontal cards or a photo gallery, with filters, a filter bar (tabs, buttons, dropdown, search box or sidebar list), a set photo-area height and pagination; doctor carousels that slide sideways or up and down; share buttons for WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and X, copy link and print.

Search

  • Several search forms, each with its own fields, operators and layout.
  • Dependent filters, such as State, then City, then Hospital.
  • Results below the form or on another page, with pagination, sorting and live updates.
  • Results can use every Doctor List option (layout, columns, card options, filter bar, “Only doctors with” and “Leave out”), and can list all published doctors before the first search.

Schedules and booking

  • Clinics with their own time zone, weekly OPD sessions (including alternate weeks and date ranges), leave, holidays and extra sessions.
  • Appointment forms with conditional fields, private file uploads and consent. A form either books a real free time or sends a request.
  • The last place in a slot can only be taken once: the time is checked again inside a database lock.
  • Staff confirm bookings, or bookings are confirmed at once. Patients are never told a request is confirmed until it is.
  • A booking page that shows the chosen doctor beside the form.

Managing appointments

  • An appointments list and calendar, a status workflow with full history, bulk changes, rescheduling and staff notes.
  • Appointments affected by schedule changes are flagged for staff.
  • Patients can cancel or ask for a new time through a private link in their email, within your deadlines.
  • CSV and Excel exports. Reminders before appointments.
  • Email templates per event and recipient (patient, doctor, clinic, admin), with merge tags and a delivery log.
  • Optional Google Sheets sync of the columns you choose.

Works your way

  • 20 shortcodes and a Shortcode Generator with live preview. Every feature works without Elementor.
  • 16 Elementor widgets with the same options and full Style-tab controls (text, boxes, buttons, inputs, photos, icons, spacing and the text shown when there is nothing to show), including your own listing cards, profile page and booking page.
  • Style settings for colours, fonts, corners, spacing, buttons, shadows and photos.
  • Import and export of your setup between sites.
  • Translation-ready.

Privacy

Patient uploads are private, submissions are visible only to authorised staff, IP addresses are stored only as a hash, and you can set a retention period. The plugin adds itself to WordPress’s Export and Erase Personal Data tools and suggests privacy policy text. It sends nothing to outside services unless you connect Google Sheets.

No plugin makes a site compliant with health-privacy law on its own. Review your hosting, policies and use of the site with someone qualified.

External services

The plugin contacts no outside service unless an administrator sets up one of the following.

Google OAuth and Google Sheets API (optional, off by default). Used only when an administrator connects Google Sheets (Orki Doctor Management → Google Sheets) to copy appointment requests into a spreadsheet.

  • When connecting with a Google account, the administrator’s browser goes to Google’s sign-in and consent page (accounts.google.com). The server then exchanges the returned code for tokens at oauth2.googleapis.com, sending the site’s OAuth client ID, client secret and redirect address.
  • When connecting with a service account, the server sends a signed token request to oauth2.googleapis.com.
  • When a feed checks a spreadsheet or syncs, the server calls sheets.googleapis.com with the spreadsheet ID and tab name. For each submission of the chosen forms, it sends only the columns the administrator ticked for that feed. Nothing is ticked by default. Staff notes and uploaded files are never offered as columns.
  • On disconnecting or uninstalling, the server asks oauth2.googleapis.com to revoke the access.

Google’s terms: https://policies.google.com/terms and https://developers.google.com/terms. Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Share buttons (only where you add a Doctor Share shortcode or widget). WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn and X buttons are plain links. Nothing is loaded from those services when the page opens. If a visitor clicks one, their browser opens that service with the doctor page’s address and title.

  • WhatsApp: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/terms-of-service and https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/privacy-policy
  • Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/terms.php and https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/
  • LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement and https://www.linkedin.com/legal/privacy-policy
  • X: https://x.com/en/tos and https://x.com/en/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, choose the ZIP, then Install Now and Activate.
  2. Open Orki Doctor Management → Dashboard and follow the Getting started steps: doctor fields, a clinic, doctors with their OPD schedule, an appointment form and a search form.
  3. Put the shortcodes on your pages. The Shortcode Generator builds them for you.
  4. On Nginx servers, protect patient uploads with the rule in Orki Doctor Management → Help. The Dashboard tells you whether the folder is protected.

The plugin’s docs folder has a full getting-started guide, a staff guide, a shortcode and settings reference, a privacy and security guide, and a checklist for checking email, Google Sheets and Elementor on your site.
sections.faq:
Do I need Elementor?

No. Every feature works through shortcodes. Elementor widgets are added when Elementor (free or Pro) is active.

Can two patients book the same time?

Only when you allow more than one patient per slot. The time is checked again inside a database lock when the form is sent, so the last place can only be taken once, even when many people book at the same moment.

Do patients get confirmed automatically?

Your choice, in Settings → Booking → Confirmation. By default staff confirm each request, and patients are told it is waiting for confirmation.

Why are emails not arriving?

WordPress’s built-in mail is often blocked or sent to spam. Use an SMTP or transactional email plugin, then send a test from Orki Doctor Management → Notifications → Settings. If WP-Cron is disabled, add the server cron job shown in Help so the email queue runs.

Can patients see each other’s details?

No. Public pages and the public REST routes show only doctors, schedules and free times. A patient’s manage page shows only their own appointment, and only through the signed link in their email.

Is data deleted when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivating never deletes anything. Deleting the plugin removes data only if you turn on Settings → Advanced → “Delete all data when the plugin is deleted”.

Does this make my site compliant with medical privacy laws?

No plugin can do that on its own. The plugin keeps patient uploads private, restricts submissions to authorised staff, hashes IP addresses, supports retention periods, and works with WordPress’s personal data export and erase tools. Your site’s policies and hosting still need review.

1.2.1

  • Security: request data (doctor fields, schedules, clinics, appointment forms, search and filters, exports) is sanitized as soon as it is read, so drafts kept after a failed save never hold unsanitized data.
  • Security: all HTML the plugin prints is escaped at output with wp_kses() and a list of the tags the plugin uses.
  • Admin notices appear only on the plugin’s own screens; the PHP and WordPress version notice only on the Plugins screen.
  • Elementor card templates load their CSS as a stylesheet instead of printing it inline.
  • New filter “dpab_now” sets the time used for reminders and the job queue (for test and staging sites).

1.2.0

  • Doctor cards: a set height for the photo area, per screen size (lists, carousels, search results, Elementor and shortcodes).
  • Doctor Search Form widget, [dpab_doctor_search] and [dpab_search_results]: results can use the Doctor List design with all its options: layout, card design (including an Elementor template), columns, card options, fields, booking button, per page, pagination, filter bar, “Only doctors with”, “Leave out” and empty text.
  • Search results: “Before a search” can list all published doctors below the form; after a search the same list shows the results. “Only doctors with” and “Leave out” apply to results and to name suggestions.
  • Results refreshed without reloading the page keep the list design; the server signs it, so a changed design is ignored.

1.1.4

  • The submission, appointment, export, email log and affected-appointment lists build their filters as one list of fixed SQL fragments with placeholders and a matching list of values. Results are unchanged.
  • Plugin header: the author link now goes to https://orki.in/, and the placeholder plugin link was removed.

1.1.3

  • Doctor search: each search condition runs its own prepared query that returns matching doctor IDs; matching, sorting and paging happen in PHP. Results and sort orders are unchanged (random order is still stable for the day, though the order itself differs from 1.1.2).
  • Booking, appointment, export, log and submission queries pass every value, including status lists, through $wpdb->prepare() placeholders.
  • [dpab_doctor_listing] and [dpab_doctor_carousel]: new leave_out attribute for doctors not to show. The 1.1 name, exclude, still works, and Elementor widgets keep their saved setting.
  • Leaving doctors out no longer uses a NOT IN query.
  • Elementor: the gallery overlay and widget button backgrounds can also use an image.
  • Clearer message when a Google OAuth client ID is pasted in the wrong format.

1.1.2

  • Saving a doctor’s field values writes each value with $wpdb->insert().
  • Translations load the standard WordPress way (wp-content/languages/plugins or translate.wordpress.org); the plugin no longer calls load_plugin_textdomain().
  • Removed two redundant suppress_filters settings on doctor lists.

1.1.1

  • Patient uploads are saved with WordPress’s upload handling (wp_handle_upload) instead of a direct file move. Files still go only to the private folder with random names and never to the Media Library.
  • The plugin ZIP no longer includes the development tests or the coding-standards config.

  • New Doctor Title, Doctor Meta and Doctor Share (shortcodes and widgets). Share opens WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn and X, copies the link or prints the page; Instagram opens the phone’s share sheet and otherwise copies the link. The Elementor widget uses Elementor’s icon library.
  • Doctor pages hide the theme’s page title, date, author line and post navigation (new setting Settings → Doctor pages → “Hide the theme’s title and post details on doctor pages”, on by default).

The Search Form widget styles labels, inputs, icons, each button, suggestions and results, and can change the heading and button texts.   • Listings: list layout and separate desktop, tablet and phone columns. Styles: button style, card shadow, photo shape and photo proportions.
  • Import / Export of configuration as a JSON file (settings, doctor fields, search and appointment forms, email templates, saved listings), with a dry run before anything changes. Doctors, patient data and Google credentials are never included.
  • Fix: booking links returned “page not found” while public profile pages were on. The doctor URL variable is renamed and permalinks are rebuilt on upgrade.
  • Fix: the same search form twice on one page no longer repeats an element id, and each copy updates its own results.
  • Database version 1.6.0: no table changes.

0.10.0

  • Build phase 10: Elementor widgets. Twelve widgets in an “Orki Doctors” category: Doctor Listing, Doctor Search Form, Doctor Profile, Doctor Field, Doctor Field Label, Doctor Field Data, Doctor Appointment Button, Appointment Form, Doctor OPD Schedule, Next Available Appointment, Available Slots and Consultation Fee. Works with Elementor Free (3.20 or newer); Pro is supported but never required.
  • Card templates: design a doctor card as an ordinary Elementor template and use it in the Doctor Listing widget for all doctors, chosen doctors or search results. Each card is rendered with its own doctor, so cards never repeat the first doctor. A “Preview doctor” setting on templates shows real data while editing.
  • New shortcodes with the same output as the widgets: [dpab_doctor_listing], [dpab_doctor_profile], [dpab_doctor_field], [dpab_field_label], [dpab_field_value], [dpab_doctor_schedule], [dpab_next_available], [dpab_available_slots], [dpab_doctor_fee]. Doctor shortcodes use the doctor of the page or listing card they are placed in.
  • The appointment button can now open the form in a dialog or below the button, besides linking to the booking page. Buttons and “doctor from context” forms inside listing cards book that card’s doctor.
  • The OPD schedule shows weekly sessions or upcoming dates with clinics and fees, and upcoming leave and holidays by date only (reasons stay private). Available slots show times only, never patient data.
  • Fix: a profile photo is no longer hidden when an earlier image field holds a value that is not an image. Field prefixes and suffixes get a small space from the value.
  • No database changes.

0.9.0

  • Build phase 9: Google Sheets (Doctor Management → Google Sheets).
  • Connect with your own Google Cloud OAuth client (you sign in on Google’s page; the plugin never asks for your password) or a service account JSON key. Client secret, refresh token, private key and access tokens are stored encrypted and never shown or sent to the browser. Disconnecting (or uninstalling the plugin) revokes and deletes them.
  • Feeds: each feed sends chosen forms to one tab of a spreadsheet. Forms and columns must be chosen explicitly; nothing is sent by default. Columns are the reference, submission number, received date, status, form, doctor, appointment date and time, clinic, fee and the forms’ own fields, with your own header text and order. File uploads and internal notes are never offered.
  • Two modes: add new rows only, or add rows and keep them up to date (status changes, new times). Rows are found again by their reference, so sorting the sheet is safe; a row removed by hand is added back on the next change. Deleting a submission clears its row (optional).
  • Values are written as plain text (formula-like text is not run). Sync runs in the background queue: temporary Google errors are retried with backoff; missing permission, a missing spreadsheet or revoked access stop at once with a clear message and an admin notice. “Send existing submissions” fills a sheet with older submissions without duplicates.
  • Sync activity log without patient data, kept 90 days. Help explains the Google Cloud steps for both ways of connecting.
  • Schema 1.5.0 (three new tables; additive).

0.8.0

  • Build phase 8: Notifications (Doctor Management → Notifications, formerly Email Notifications) with Templates, Delivery log and Settings tabs.
  • Email templates per event: request received, booking received, awaiting confirmation, confirmed, declined, cancelled, cancelled by the patient, rescheduled, reminder, new time requested and completed. Each event can have several templates, each for chosen forms or all forms, and each can be switched on or off, duplicated or deleted.
  • Recipients per template in To, Cc and Bcc: the patient, staff, the doctor (from a chosen doctor email field), the clinic, or other addresses.
  • Editor with subject, heading, message, button, footer, designed (HTML, responsive) or plain-text format, click-to-insert tags, fallback text for empty tags, a chosen list of fields for {{fields}}, a live preview with sample data or a real submission, and “send a test”.
  • Safety: submitted values are escaped; unknown tags are refused when saving and never show braces; staff-only tags (admin link, internal notes, history) cannot be used in emails that reach the patient; the patient manage link never goes to staff; patients only see public doctor fields.
  • Delivery log: one entry per recipient with a masked address, status (queued, sent to mailer, failed, skipped, delivered when an SMTP plugin confirms it), attempts and the mailer’s error; filters; failed emails can be sent again. Kept 180 days and deleted with the submission. Also shown on each submission.
  • Existing wording is carried over on upgrade (sites that customised it keep plain-text emails); new sites get designed emails. Jobs queued before the upgrade are still sent.
  • The form builder warns when patient templates apply but the form has no patient email field.
  • Schema 1.4.0 (two new tables; additive).

0.7.0

  • Build phase 7: Appointments screen (Doctor Management → Appointments) with a list (filters by doctor, clinic, status, dates; patient names; bulk status changes that report each refusal) and a month calendar with a day agenda.
  • Rescheduling: staff move an appointment to another free time (any of the doctor’s clinics) from the appointment page. The new time is checked inside the booking locks (tested with 12 parallel moves and a new booking competing for one place: exactly one won); fee, clinic and the submission’s values are updated and the history records the move.
  • Patient manage link: patient emails include a private link to a Manage appointment page (created automatically) where patients cancel or choose a new time within the cancellation and reschedule deadlines. Under staff confirmation a new time is a request that staff approve or decline from the list or the appointment page; the original slot stays booked meanwhile.
  • Reminders: emails 24 and 2 hours before confirmed appointments (configurable); moved or cancelled appointments never get stale reminders.
  • Workflow emails: rescheduled, cancelled, request declined, reminder, change request received (patient) and change requested (staff), plus a staff notice when a patient cancels. Templates on the Email Notifications screen.
  • Affected appointments: when leave, a holiday, a closure, a removed session or a deactivated clinic leaves an upcoming appointment without a session, it is marked “Schedule changed” (notice on the Appointments screen and the doctor’s page). Staff reschedule, cancel or keep it; nothing is changed automatically. Sessions at a deactivated clinic no longer offer slots.
  • Export (Doctor Management → Export): XLSX or CSV of requests and bookings with filters (form, doctor, clinic, status, appointment or received dates), chosen columns in a chosen order including any form field, optional internal notes and IDs. XLSX has real dates, times and numbers, a frozen header and filters; formula-like text is kept as text. The column choice is remembered per user.
  • Schema 1.3.0 (additive).

0.6.0

  • Build phase 6: Appointment Form Builder with 26 field types, including booking fields (doctor, clinic, appointment type, date and time slot, fee display), uploads, consent, hidden fields, headings and instruction blocks. Drag-and-drop ordering, duplicate forms and fields, conditional show/hide rules (checked in the browser and again on the server) and a live preview.
  • Doctor per form: none, a fixed doctor, the doctor whose page or button opened the form (signed link, cannot be swapped), or the patient’s choice.
  • Booking: a form with a “Date and time slot” field shows a calendar of available dates and free times from the OPD schedule. The server recomputes the slot, fee, session and timezone and books inside an InnoDB row lock; tested with 16 parallel bookings for one place (exactly one succeeds) and for three places (exactly three).
  • Confirmation policy (automatic or staff review), slot holds while a request waits (until review, for N hours, or none), active-bookings-per-patient limit, references in a configurable format, idempotent submissions (double clicks never book twice).
  • Appointment statuses with a fixed transition map and full history: awaiting approval, confirmed, checked in, in consultation, completed, cancelled by patient or clinic, reschedule requested, no-show, rejected.
  • Request forms are clearly not appointments: patients are told so on screen and by email.
  • Spam protection: honeypot, signed timestamp (too fast / too old), per-visitor rate limit, and a dpab_validate_spam filter for CAPTCHA add-ons.
  • Private uploads: real file-type checks, size and count limits, random names outside the Media Library, staff-only downloads with nonce and nosniff headers.
  • Submissions screen: filters by form, doctor, status and date, search by reference, detail view with values, files, appointment status changes, history, internal notes and email log, delete.
  • Email notifications through a background queue with retries: staff notice, patient receipt (“not yet confirmed”), and a confirmation email when an appointment is confirmed. New booking templates on the Email Notifications screen.
  • Submission retention (Settings → Privacy) now deletes old submissions daily, keeping bookings with upcoming appointments.
  • Forms work without JavaScript (plain post and redirect with errors shown next to fields).

0.5.1

  • Fixed: with “Show all doctors before a search” turned off, an empty search or the Reset button still listed every doctor. Nothing is listed now until at least one filter is chosen.
  • New: suggestions while typing in search text boxes (doctor names and searchable values for keyword boxes, stored values for other text fields), with keyboard support. Can be turned off per field.
  • New: Vertical / Horizontal choice for the search form layout, shown at the top of the Fields tab. Horizontal places fields side by side with the button at the end and stacks on phones.
  • New: fields with several values (checkboxes, multi-select) can use a dropdown (pick one value); dropdown is now the default input for list fields.

0.5.0

  • Build phase 5: Search Form Builder. Create any number of search forms from doctor fields marked searchable, with a live preview of the visitor’s form.
  • Operators matched to each field type: exact match, contains, starts with, greater than, less than, numeric range, date range, multiple values (any of / all of), plus a keyword field across the name and searchable text.
  • Per-field label, placeholder, input type, required, width on desktop and phone, default value, icon, order, visibility (hidden fixed filters) and reset behaviour; option lists from the field, doctor data, a typed list or a taxonomy.
  • Dependent fields of any depth (e.g. Country → State → City → Hospital, Specialization → Doctor) from doctor data, a manual mapping or matching doctors, with AJAX option loading, invalid selections cleared, circular-dependency checks, a dependency check and clear error messages.
  • Results below the form, on a chosen page or updated in place (AJAX with shareable URLs and Back button support); sorting, pagination that keeps every filter, result count, configurable no-results message and reset button.
  • Shortcodes [dpab_doctor_search id=””] and [dpab_search_results form=””]. Only published, public doctors are ever searched or offered as options.
  • Fixed: lists of several values now show a space after the comma.

0.4.0

  • Build phase 4: clinics and locations with their own timezone, default fee and booking rules.
  • OPD schedule builder on each doctor: weekly sessions, every 2–4 weeks from a starting date, chosen weeks of the month (1st–5th, last), specific dates, valid-from/until ranges, breaks, appointment length, gap, patients per slot and per session, fee, currency, appointment type and priority, with a live slot preview.
  • Leave, public holidays, clinic holidays, emergency closures, cancelled sessions, extra sessions, rescheduled sessions, temporary schedules and fee changes, with documented precedence.
  • Slot engine: clinic timezones and daylight saving, minimum notice, booking window, open-from/until dates, same-day cutoff, slot, session and daily capacity; a doctor is never offered in two places at the same real time.
  • OPD Calendar (month, week, agenda) for all doctors, with holiday and closure management.
  • Public availability REST endpoints (published doctors only, no patient data, rate limited).
  • Database 1.1.0: clinics, schedule rules and schedule exceptions tables.

0.3.0

  • Build phase 3: Doctor Field Builder with 24 field types, drag-and-drop ordering, searchable icon library, per-type settings, duplicate, deactivate and safe delete with CSV export.
  • Doctor editor built from the administrator’s fields, with server-side validation, draft and publish rules, media pickers, repeaters and a profile preview.
  • Doctors list with dynamic columns, search across field values, sorting by field, filters, bulk publish, unpublish and duplicate.
  • Doctor titles follow the chosen primary display field.

0.2.0

  • Build phase 2: plugin foundation. Database schema (11 tables) with migrations, capabilities and optional Clinic Staff role, doctor post type, settings framework, email settings, admin menu with 13 screens, Dashboard health checks, private upload folder, security helpers, REST base, uninstall with opt-in data removal.

  • The last place in a slot can only be taken once: the time is checked again inside a database lock.
  • Staff confirm bookings, or bookings are confirmed at once. Patients are never told a request is confirmed until it is.
  • A booking page that shows the chosen doctor beside the form.

Managing appointments

  • An appointments list and calendar, a status workflow with full history, bulk changes, rescheduling and staff notes.
  • Appointments affected by schedule changes are flagged for staff.
  • Patients can cancel or ask for a new time through a private link in their email, within your deadlines.
  • CSV and Excel exports. Reminders before appointments.
  • Email templates per event and recipient (patient, doctor, clinic, admin), with merge tags and a delivery log.
  • Optional Google Sheets sync of the columns you choose.

Works your way

  • 20 shortcodes and a Shortcode Generator with live preview. Every feature works without Elementor.
  • 16 Elementor widgets with the same options and full Style-tab controls (text, boxes, buttons, inputs, photos, icons, spacing and the text shown when there is nothing to show), including your own listing cards, profile page and booking page.
  • Style settings for colours, fonts, corners, spacing, buttons, shadows and photos.
  • Import and export of your setup between sites.
  • Translation-ready.

Privacy

Patient uploads are private, submissions are visible only to authorised staff, IP addresses are stored only as a hash, and you can set a retention period. The plugin adds itself to WordPress’s Export and Erase Personal Data tools and suggests privacy policy text. It sends nothing to outside services unless you connect Google Sheets.

No plugin makes a site compliant with health-privacy law on its own. Review your hosting, policies and use of the site with someone qualified.

External services

The plugin contacts no outside service unless an administrator sets up one of the following.

Google OAuth and Google Sheets API (optional, off by default). Used only when an administrator connects Google Sheets (Orki Doctor Management → Google Sheets) to copy appointment requests into a spreadsheet.

  • When connecting with a Google account, the administrator’s browser goes to Google’s sign-in and consent page (accounts.google.com). The server then exchanges the returned code for tokens at oauth2.googleapis.com, sending the site’s OAuth client ID, client secret and redirect address.
  • When connecting with a service account, the server sends a signed token request to oauth2.googleapis.com.
  • When a feed checks a spreadsheet or syncs, the server calls sheets.googleapis.com with the spreadsheet ID and tab name. For each submission of the chosen forms, it sends only the columns the administrator ticked for that feed. Nothing is ticked by default. Staff notes and uploaded files are never offered as columns.
  • On disconnecting or uninstalling, the server asks oauth2.googleapis.com to revoke the access.

Google’s terms: https://policies.google.com/terms and https://developers.google.com/terms. Privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Share buttons (only where you add a Doctor Share shortcode or widget). WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn and X buttons are plain links. Nothing is loaded from those services when the page opens. If a visitor clicks one, their browser opens that service with the doctor page’s address and title.

  • WhatsApp: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/terms-of-service and https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/privacy-policy
  • Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/terms.php and https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/
  • LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement and https://www.linkedin.com/legal/privacy-policy
  • X: https://x.com/en/tos and https://x.com/en/privacy
